text: Replace pointwise binary cross-entropy with within-user pairwise Bayesian Personalized Ranking updates on experiment 1's additive-plus-16-dimensional interaction logits, while initializing both user and video embedding tables with small seeded normal noise (standard deviation 0.01) so the interaction receives nonzero gradients. Sample one long-view-positive and one long-view-negative impression from the same eligible user, skip users without both classes, and optimize softplus of the negative score margin. Keep additive weights, model dimensions, optimizer settings, data split, validation checkpointing, and within-user ranking evaluation unchanged. This tests whether an activated personalized interaction trained directly for relative ordering improves GAUC and nDCG@5 over the zero-initialized pointwise interaction model.
rationale: The rejected BPR proposal retained zero initialization, making both embedding tables receive zero pairwise gradients and reducing training to the additive model. This replacement explicitly uses a deterministic small random initialization to break that symmetry before applying the ranking-aligned BPR objective, allowing the 16-dimensional user-video interaction to learn. Pair sampling remains bounded by drawing one positive and one negative per eligible user, while the architecture, split, optimizer controls, checkpointing, and official within-user metrics remain fixed. The combined intervention is necessary to test the intended mechanism rather than reproduce experiments 1 and 2; the main risk is that changing initialization alongside the loss complicates attribution, but the comparison directly evaluates whether an activated interaction trained for ordering provides ranking gains.
